iterations.theme: Celebration of victory in the derby against Dinamo, difficult weather conditions and refereeing controversies

sections.subtitle: Great victory in impossible conditions: Hajduk fight in the Poljud deluge
sections.screenshot_description: Vinko Dubravica in the studio explains how the entire Hajduk team played combatively like Ivan Gudelj
sections.content:
The opening moments of the analysis passed in a celebratory mood following Hajduk's triumph over Dinamo in the derby played under an extreme downpour. Host Marjan brings euphoric energy into the show, emphasizing the relief that after a long time the derby can be analyzed with a smile, rather than with sorrow and tears. Commenting on the conditions at Poljud, Marjan vividly describes how the rainy Saturday evening looked like the sunniest day to the fans, even though on the east stand the roof was leaking water so the spectators had to huddle in the aisles and on the stairs, while the north stand completely took off their shirts and carried the team to victory.

Vinko Dubravica recalled the previews before the match in which it was predicted that it would be played in heavy mud and that Hajduk did not have a profile of player in its squad like the legendary 'number eight' Ivan Gudelj. But, according to Dubravica's judgment, on the soaked Poljud pitch the entire Hajduk team functioned through joint effort as one Ivan Gudelj. Marjan completely agreed with that assessment, emphasizing that the commitment was flawless and that not a single technical error could be faulted to the players because they fought tirelessly for every ball in conditions that in the second half crossed the boundaries of regular football and turned into real water polo.

sections.subtitle: Complete control of the derby: Dinamo clueless on the soaked pitch
sections.screenshot_description: Analysis of Hajduk's tactical dominance and chances created on the soaked Poljud pitch
sections.content:
Reflecting on the events on the pitch before the field turned completely into a swimming pool, Vinko Dubravica points out that throughout the entire match Dinamo did not show that they could seriously threaten Hajduk without direct errors by the home defense. According to his view, Hajduk was the one dictating the tempo, controlling the course of the match, and looking far more organized. Although Dinamo stumbled into the leading goal, the guests from Zagreb had no answers for Hajduk's aggressiveness and spatial coverage.

Marjan confirmed that thesis, recalling the more mature chances of the 'Whites', especially highlighting Michele Šego's early sitter as early as the fifth minute of the match. He emphasized that Hajduk was half a step faster in reactions and duels throughout the entire game. Dubravica also ironically looked back at Dinamo's center-back McKenzie, thanking him for clumsy reactions that helped the Split team reach a deserved lead. Spectators also joined the conversation with congratulations and donations, confirming how much this victory relieved the entire Hajduk public.

sections.subtitle: A brake on euphoria: Victory in the derby counts only with a celebration in Varaždin
sections.screenshot_description: Shot from the studio in which the interlocutors warn of caution and the necessity of focusing on the championship
sections.content:
Despite the great celebration, the interlocutors in the studio deliberately pulled the brake when it came to long-term conclusions. Vinko Dubravica notes that after a series of traumatic seasons, Hajduk fans carry a kind of caution and subconsciously defend themselves from excessive celebration so that painful disappointment would not follow. Marjan recalls the cold fact: only the ninth championship round has been played, 27 matches remain until the end of the season, and nothing has been won yet. Nevertheless, he emphasizes the great importance of this triumph for coach Gonzalo Garcia, who finally relieved the pressure and registered a victory in the derby, during which he completely lost his voice from vocally leading the team.

Frane followed up on the atmosphere in the city and at the stadium, emphasizing that before and after the match there was no unrealistic euphoria, but rather a mature and positive energy prevailed without the usual nervous pressure from the stands. The interlocutors drew a parallel with historic matches, such as the one against Anderlecht, when dramatic finishes emotionally drained the crowd. The conclusion is clear: three points against Dinamo will gain their true weight only if Varaždin is defeated in the next round. Marjan openly admitted that the upcoming European clash against Ajax is not even in his thoughts because the championship is the club's sole and absolute priority.

sections.subtitle: Sharp criticism of Igor Pajač: Double standards and the non-existent sending off of Kačavenda
sections.screenshot_description: Host Marjan gestures while explaining contentious refereeing decisions and fouls
sections.content:
The refereeing topic occupied the central part of the discussion, with the interlocutors putting forward a series of heavy accusations against head referee Igor Pajač. Frane opened the question of the offensive foul called in favor of Dinamo's goalkeeper, noting that by reviewing the footage he found no basis for stopping play. However, far greater wrath was provoked by the refereeing treatment of Dinamo's attacker Kačavenda. According to Marjan's and Frane's judgment, Kačavenda committed fouls worthy of two clear yellow cards already in the early phase of the match, which is why he should not have been on the pitch at all for the remainder of the game.

Marjan drew a direct comparison with the match in Osijek, where Pajač sent off the young Brajković without hesitation for significantly milder tackles, while at Poljud he turned a blind eye to the player of the visiting team. Vinko Dubravica also recalled the situation with booting the ball away after the whistle—a foul for which Marko Livaja was previously rigorously punished with a second yellow card, while Dinamo's player got away without a warning in an identical situation. Host Marjan concluded sharply that the officiating was tendentious and condemned the media appearances of Bruno Marić, considering it unacceptable that a narrative about Dinamo supposedly being wronged is created in the public sphere.

sections.subtitle: Poljud drainage under the deluge test and Torcida's tribute to Dino Dvornik
sections.screenshot_description: Depiction of the discussion about the condition of the Poljud pitch and choreography on the north stand
sections.content:
The issue of Poljud's infrastructure arose after the pitch was flooded with water puddles in the second half. Marjan expressed surprise at the speed with which the water accumulated, but Vinko Dubravica explained that no drainage system in the world could absorb such an amount of precipitation that continuously fell for hours. He recalled an earlier match against Istra, when the pitch recovered very quickly the moment the rain stopped, emphasizing that Saturday's weather conditions were truly extreme.

In the more relaxed part of the conversation, Torcida was praised for an extraordinary choreography dedicated to the legendary Split musician Dino Dvornik with the message 'Ništa kontra Splita'. Marjan shared an emotional personal childhood anecdote with the viewers, recalling that he grew up in the same building entrance with brothers Dino and Dean Dvornik. He recounted how in their youth they played improvised baseball on a dirt pitch until they smashed windows on a nearby school, concluding that Dino Dvornik was and remained the true king of Split whose spirit perfectly matched the ambiance of this dramatic derby.

sections.subtitle: Fifteen minutes of stoppage time without a feel for football: Pajač's loss of control
sections.screenshot_description: Vinko Dubravica criticizes the refereeing profile and lack of understanding of the game of football
sections.content:
The final segment of the first part of the analysis was dedicated to the referee's stoppage time of as much as 12 minutes, which extended to more than 15 minutes due to additional stoppages. Frane problematized the referee's decision to extend the match at moments when playing conditions had become completely irregular, questioning what the point was of letting the game go on in deep water instead of bringing the match to an earlier close. Although interruptions due to pyrotechnics in the stands justified more time, Frane considers that the handling of the endgame was chaotic.

Vinko Dubravica offered a deeper analysis of the refereeing profile of Igor Pajač, asserting that he belongs to the category of referees who simply do not have a 'feeling' for the game of football. In Dubravica's opinion, Pajač does not feel the pulse of the pitch, the rhythm of the match, nor the psychology of the players, which causes him to serially stumble from mistake to mistake. Marjan agreed with that assessment, adding that Pajač's decisions are not accidental but part of a broader system, though he cynically noted that Hajduk has a distinctly positive record of derby wins with that referee. The conversation concluded with a reminder of Beljo's unsanctioned elbow from the beginning of the match, rounding off the story of refereeing controversies before moving on to ratings of individual players.

iterations.theme: Analysis of the team by position: goalkeeper, defense, and midfield

sections.subtitle: Assessment of Silić's performance and insecurity in the back line
sections.screenshot_description: Vinko Dubravica and Marjan discuss the interventions and clearances of goalkeeper Silić.
sections.content:
Commenting on individual performances on the pitch, the interlocutors opened the analysis by dissecting the performance of goalkeeper Silić. Frane immediately noted that the young shot-stopper did not inspire his usual confidence during this match, highlighting a situation from the first half in which he made mistakes in clearances and failed to spot open teammates on the wing.

Marjan and Vinko Dubravica agreed that Silić's performances were not at the level of security he had accustomed fans to in the preceding period. Particular emphasis was placed on weak clearances and low goal kicks along the ground that on several occasions went straight to the feet of opposing players. As for the conceded goal, Vinko stated that Silić could perhaps have reacted more decisively with a timely charge out for the cross, although it was concluded that the responsibility lay in an entire series of errors in the positioning of the central defense. Nevertheless, it was pointed out that Silić saved several awkward shots and managed to see out the match without fatal consequences.

sections.subtitle: Center-back tandem under the magnifying glass and calls for more playing time for Hadžikadunić
sections.screenshot_description: Marjan gestures while explaining the center-back hierarchy and the security that Hadžikadunić brings.
sections.content:
The transition to the center-back positions brought a sharp debate about the profiles and output of the defenders. Marjan unhesitatingly pointed out that Hadžikadunić made the best impression on him among the center-backs, despite the fact that he spent the least time on the pitch. He was fascinated by the security that this defender brings into the game—from clearing dangerous situations and clearances in front of his own goal, to dominance in aerial duels where he regularly won headers.

A controversy arose in the studio around the fact that a player of such renown and physical predispositions starts the derby on the bench, especially when a physically powerful striker like Beljo was on the other side. Vinko Dubravica agreed with the assessment that Hadžikadunić should be an unquestioned choice in the starting 11 around whom the back line is built, while he criticized certain tactical maneuvers and reckless handoffs performed by other center-backs before the conceded goal.

sections.subtitle: Infrastructural reality: Flooded Poljud and the announcement of the Mediterranean Games
sections.screenshot_description: Shot of the interlocutors as they discuss infrastructure projects in Split and the stadium issue.
sections.content:
The catastrophic conditions on the pitch and the flood in the stands opened the broader topic of Split's sports infrastructure. Spurred by fan comments and rumors that Split could host the Mediterranean Games again in 2031, the participants analyzed what that event would mean for club and city facilities.

Marjan expressed a clear stance: the solution for the Mediterranean Games must not jeopardize the construction of a modern football stadium at Poljud. He proposed that an adequate athletics stadium with 20,000 seats and a tartan track be built at Park mladeži to serve athletes permanently, while Poljud should be freed of the running track and transformed into a true football home. Along with the stadium issues, he also recalled the catastrophic shortage of indoor swimming pools in Split, a city that nurtures an exceptional tradition of water polo and swimming sports, and whose athletes train under extremely difficult conditions in winter.

sections.subtitle: The team's flanks: Hrgović's maturity and reliability on the right side
sections.screenshot_description: Frane and Marjan analyze Hrgović's tactical role and his crossing.
sections.content:
The analysis of the full-backs brought unanimous recognition to Šimun Hrgović, who played a mature and tactically responsible match. The participants underlined his key attacking contribution, primarily the precise crosses that created confusion in the opponent's penalty box and directly created goals. Marjan observed that Hrgović has evidently matured and plays without his former nervousness, fear, and throwing his hands up in the air.

Vinko Dubravica and Frane pointed out that Hrgović's cooperation with the wingers functioned smoothly, which significantly eased his defensive duties as well. On the opposite side of the pitch, the simple and pragmatic performance of the right-back was praised. Although even more is expected from him going forward in the future, it was assessed that he did his part of the job properly, combatively, and without overcomplicating things, sticking firmly to his tactical discipline.

sections.subtitle: Midfield: Del Moral's defensive rampart and control of the center of the pitch
sections.screenshot_description: Marjan emphasizes the importance of the defensive destruction carried out by Del Moral.
sections.content:
The center of the pitch was the area where Hajduk turned the match, and the central figure of the defensive part of the midfield was Del Moral. Although he experienced an awkward slip and an ankle injury right at the opening of the match, he gritted his teeth and did immense work destroying the opponent's play. Marjan emphasized that Del Moral is not the profile of player from whom forward creation is expected, but his role as a sweeper and tactical safeguard in front of the center-backs was crucial.

Vinko Dubravica highlighted his brilliant reading of space, positioning, and impressive number of won aerial duels in the danger zone. The interlocutors agreed that it was precisely through that firmness in the center that every Dinamo idea through the half-spaces was neutralized. As long as Del Moral watches the back and takes on the dirty work defensively, the more creative midfielders gain freedom of action going forward, which hit the jackpot in this match.

sections.subtitle: Profiling player roles in the midfield and the need for rotations
sections.screenshot_description: Interlocutors in a lively discussion about player profiles, tactical options, and rotations in a tight schedule.
sections.content:
The final part of the midfield analysis turned into a debate on player profiling and the distribution of roles. The question of balance between aggressiveness, speed of distribution, and tactical responsibility was raised. Marjan emphasized that the team suffers when midfielders unnecessarily slow down ball circulation, which is why he advocates a more modern approach with more vertical solutions, while Vinko Dubravica underlined that the roles of defensive midfielder and 'number eight' must be strictly delimited depending on the opponent.

Frane recalled the hellish rhythm awaiting the team in the coming weeks—league commitments intertwined with European tests will require rotation of the entire squad. The interlocutors concluded that the coach must not force exclusively a handful of proven names while his alternatives sit unused on the bench. Every player on the roster will have to make his contribution and find a precisely defined role if the club wants to maintain continuity of results on multiple fronts.

iterations.theme: Analysis of attacking output, substitutions, and tactical game management

sections.subtitle: Wingers' output: Dynamic Šotiček and Bamba as player of the match
sections.screenshot_description: Host Marjan emphasizes that winger Bamba was the key individual of the derby at Poljud.
sections.content:
Analyzing the winger positions, the interlocutors agreed that the wide attackers did an extraordinary job in extremely demanding conditions. Frane opened the discussion by emphasizing that both Šotiček and Bamba deserved the highest marks for the combative spirit and energy shown. In Šotiček's case, he particularly regretted the missed chance where he slipped on the soaked pitch, noting that a goal would have been the crowning achievement of his tireless running in both directions.

Marjan emphasized that Šotiček, in tandem with Hrgović on the left side, appears exceptionally well-coordinated and dangerous, although an extra touch occasionally happens to him that he must eliminate from his game. When it comes to Bamba, Marjan declared him player of the match without hesitation. He highlighted his impressive skill moves, creating numerical superiority through isolations, and the key goal that decided the match, with a remark that Bamba created several great chances that his teammates failed to convert.

Vinko Dubravica followed up with an acknowledgment that Bamba's approach to the jersey and team tasks reached a level that deserves full respect. He concluded that no one has the right to complain to Bamba about minor mistakes anymore because he leaves his heart on the pitch, and his sincere joy after scoring the goal best illustrates how much the team's success means to him.

sections.subtitle: Šego's performance: missed chances and the key assist
sections.screenshot_description: Vinko Dubravica comments on Šego's contribution and his assist that decided the derby.
sections.content:
The performance of striker Šego elicited divided, but very passionate reactions from the analysts. Marjan stated bluntly that Šego, had he not registered the assist for the winning goal, would have been among the lowest-rated players of the match. Although no one can dispute his high pressing and immense energy expenditure, Marjan recalled incomprehensible lapses in the attacking phase—primarily the missed sitter as early as the fifth minute of the match from Bamba's cross, as well as technical difficulties in receiving and shielding the ball with his back turned to goal.

Frane noted that Šego spent most of the second half on the edge of or in offside, struggling with timing and positioning between the opposing center-backs. Nevertheless, he pointed out that at the crucial moment he managed to ideally cushion and lay off the ball for Bamba's shot, which was the move that decided the derby.

Vinko Dubravica pointed out that Šego plays in specific bursts—sometimes looking like a top-class player, and sometimes falling into series of incomprehensible misses. Despite all the fluctuations and misses that could have cost the team dearly, Vinko concluded that everything must be forgiven him because of that assist in the derby, as the victory over the biggest rival washed away all previous mistakes.

sections.subtitle: Discussion on Marko Livaja's playing time in difficult conditions
sections.screenshot_description: Frane and Marjan discuss whether Marko Livaja should have gotten a chance in the closing stages of the soaked derby.
sections.content:
The status and non-entry of Marko Livaja into the game opened a tactical debate among the interlocutors. Frane expressed incomprehension over the coaching staff's decision to leave Livaja on the bench, especially in the second-half period when the team sorely needed someone capable of receiving the ball under pressure, shielding it, and preserving possession in difficult conditions on the pitch. He pointed out that Livaja did not even warm up in the closing stages, which indicates that there was a clear intention not to use him at all.

Marjan raised the question of why Šego had to complete all ninety minutes on a pitch that turned into mud and a pool of water, when it was visible that he was completely exhausted and that in the closing stages he failed to adequately clear dangerous situations in front of his own goal. He believes that in such water polo conditions a profile like Livaja could have made a difference thanks to supreme technique, ball control, and the ability to play 'futsal'.

Nevertheless, analyzing the broader picture, the interlocutors left room for the possibility that the soaked pitch was too great a risk for Livaja's physical condition, but it was concluded that Hajduk needs both strikers in rotation and that it would be optimal to find a model in which both have a clear and defined role.

sections.subtitle: Contribution of players off the bench: Šutalo, Kadušić, and Melnjak
sections.screenshot_description: Shot in which analysts evaluate the output of players who came off the bench in the second half.
sections.content:
The introduction of substitutes in the second half brought necessary freshness and stability. Šutalo came on for the exhausted Šotiček, and Marjan and Frane praised his entry onto the right wing. Šutalo immediately showed verticality, tried a shot at the near post, and brought much-needed discipline to the defensive phase, which confirmed that he can be seriously counted on without the need for complicated rotations on the wing positions.

Special praise went to Kadušić, who replaced the yellow-carded center-back. Marjan and Vinko Dubravica agreed that Kadušić brought calm and security in aerial duels, clearing high balls that fell into the penalty box in the dramatic endgame. In their judgment, Kadušić demonstrates through his performances that he possesses the quality for the starting eleven and deserves regular playing time at the center-back position.

Melnjak's entry into the game instead of Šotiček was also evaluated as a timely and useful tactical maneuver. Frane described him as an experienced fighter who plowed through the left side of the pitch with relentless sliding tackles and energy, while Don Kero added physical toughness in the midfield in the very closing stages and prevented the opponent's attempts to organize attacks.

sections.subtitle: Rating of coach Garcia and the timing of tactical substitutions
sections.screenshot_description: Host Marjan analyzes the match management by coach Garcia and reactions from the bench.
sections.content:
The match management by coach Garcia was dissected through the prism of the first big victory in the derby. Marjan emphasized that Garcia made a huge step forward because he managed to turn the result around after conceding a goal, which is a scenario Hajduk had not executed in such duels for a long time. He was particularly impressed by the coach's engagement along the touchline, noticing that Garcia literally lost his voice while leading the team and cheering on the players in every duel.

Vinko Dubravica touched upon the timing of the substitutions, admitting that Garcia once again waited a long time before making his first moves off the bench. While the opponent used a larger number of substitutions early, Garcia made moves only around the 75th minute. However, Vinko compared this to a basketball endgame in which the coach deliberately times the entry of fresh forces for overtime and the final fifteen minutes of battle in water and mud, which ultimately proved correct.

It was concluded that this victory brings Garcia much-needed peace and immense self-confidence. The success in the derby lifted the atmosphere within the dressing room, but the analysts underlined that the real test of maturity follows already in the upcoming fixtures, where Garcia must confirm a winning mentality and continuity in collecting points.

sections.subtitle: Fatigue, summary of the atmosphere from the stands, and Frane's sign-off
sections.screenshot_description: Frane talks about the emotional and physical exhaustion and says goodbye before leaving the show.
sections.content:
Entering the third hour of the marathon podcast, the interlocutors looked back at the atmosphere at Poljud and the physical exhaustion after an extremely demanding day. Frane described the ambiance at the stadium as fantastic, emphasizing that despite the heavy downpour almost 25 thousand fans created an incredible energy without unnecessary nervousness or whistling. He praised Torcida's choreography and the overall synergy of the east, west, and north stands, which breathed as one body.

Admitting that his eyes were closing from fatigue and lack of sleep, Frane announced his departure to go to sleep, emphasizing that the team brought the Hajduk faithful the best possible reason to celebrate. He only warned that one must not fall into false euphoria and that the most important thing is to maintain focus on the championship and the upcoming away match in Varaždin.

Marjan and Vinko Dubravica thanked Frane for his participation and saw him off along with birthday wishes to loyal viewers, concluding that the derby drew the last atoms of strength from everyone present, but that the feeling of triumph in such conditions is the best reward for the spilled sweat and endured stress.

iterations.theme: Psychological significance of the victory, media reverberations, and looking toward Europe

sections.subtitle: Psychological turning point for Hajduk and unrest in Dinamo's camp
sections.screenshot_description: Host Marjan and interlocutor Vinko Dubravica analyze in the studio the psychological impact of the derby victory on both teams.
sections.content:
The victory in water polo conditions at Poljud marked a huge psychological boost for the Split team, but also opened cracks in the camp of the biggest rival. Host Marjan, in conversation with Vinko Dubravica, points out that the roles have completely reversed. While in Split a triumph achieved after a comeback is being celebrated, turmoil has begun at Maksimir, and sharp media criticisms are directed at Dinamo's coaching staff and management, especially at the expense of coach Mario Kovačević and club leadership.

Vinko Dubravica emphasizes that unrest is a natural state for Hajduk to which the Split public is accustomed, whereas at Maksimir such a development of events causes real panic because they are not used to pressure and insecurity. He compares this victory to the key second leg against Polish Raków, rating it as a kind of 'kick in the butt' that instills much-needed self-confidence in the players and coach Gonzalo Garcia.

The special value of the derby lies in the fact that 'double three points' were won—three extra points for Hajduk and three fewer points for the direct competitor, which drastically changes the dynamics on the table compared to the previous season. The team showed character by bouncing back from a deficit after a heavy defeat at Rujevica and a lengthy international break.

sections.subtitle: The match against Ajax as relief and the imperative against Varaždin
sections.screenshot_description: Vinko Dubravica gestures while explaining the importance of the league match compared to the European clash.
sections.content:
Although the fan base eagerly awaits the arrival of the famous Dutch giant at Poljud, a clear stance on club priorities prevails in the studio. Vinko Dubravica and Marjan see the match with Ajax in the Conference League primarily as a reward for past efforts and an opportunity for team bonding, rather than as a fixture under the imperative of a result.

- **European clash without pressure**: Against Ajax, a sensation is not expected nor should a defeat cause drama, but rather the goal is to play manly, unburdened, and without fear, resembling historic encounters against heavy favorites.
- **Absolute league focus**: The true weight of the points won in the derby will be confirmed exclusively in Sunday's league fixture against Varaždin.

Marjan underlines that a possible slip-up against Varaždin would completely erase the euphoria created by toppling Dinamo. The team must show maturity and learn to win with continuity, without falling into the traps of confidence that easily turns into underestimating the opponent in the domestic championship.

sections.subtitle: Media comments on the derby and a review of refereeing analysts
sections.screenshot_description: Marjan comments on newspaper headlines and public appearances of refereeing analysts after the derby.
sections.content:
The analysis of the match's media reception provoked a heated discussion in the studio, primarily due to the treatment that refereeing analysts and certain newspaper commentators enjoy in the public space. Marjan and Vinko Dubravica addressed comments claiming that Dinamo was wronged by Igor Pajač's officiating, particularly highlighting the appearances of Bruno Marić.

Vinko shared a quip from one of the viewers who compared Marić's advocacy of honesty to Tomo Horvatinčić's lectures on traffic safety, which drew loud laughter in the studio. The interlocutors expressed dismay at the fact that such figures are given a media platform at all in relevant sports publications and broadcasts, calling it a systematic ignoring of obvious errors to Hajduk's detriment.

As the height of absurdity, a review by football coach Ilija Lončarević in the press was cited, in which he stated that 'Dinamo showed in an hour of play that it was the better and more assured team, even though it showed this with nothing concrete'. Such contradictory constructions were evaluated in the studio as further proof of media efforts to diminish Hajduk's clean and deserved victory.

sections.subtitle: National team status: arguments for calling up Hrgović and Šotiček
sections.screenshot_description: Close-up of Marjan as he argues the reasons why Šimun Hrgović should receive a national team call-up.
sections.content:
To a viewer's question about whether young attacker Marin Šotiček and left-back Šimun Hrgović deserve a call-up to the senior national team of Croatia, the interlocutors offered a clear differentiation. While they recognize exceptional potential in both, their current status on the national team stage requires a different approach.

Marjan pointed out that Hrgović has already at this moment earned a preliminary call-up or a direct call-up from head coach Zlatko Dalić, emphasizing the chronic deficit of quality full-backs in the national side. He noted that in the Zagreb media an aggressive campaign for going to a major tournament would already have been waged for weeks if Hrgović by any chance wore Dinamo's jersey, drawing a parallel with the treatment certain players from Maksimir and Gradski vrt had.

On the other hand, on the question of Marin Šotiček, both Marjan and Vinko share the view that it is still too early for the senior side. They believe that Šotiček must first gain stability and continuity in the U-21 youth national team and prove the ability to decide matches on his own against teams like Slaven Belupo, Istra, or Lokomotiva, before skipping steps and stepping into the circle of the Vatreni.

sections.subtitle: Strategic approach to the Conference League group stage
sections.screenshot_description: Vinko Dubravica analyzes the European draw and potential opponents of Hajduk in the group stage.
sections.content:
Looking ahead to the schedule in the Conference League, the commentators dissected the dynamics of European challenges in detail. They rate the opener against a big name like Ajax at Poljud as an excellent scenario precisely because of the absence of pressure—any positive outcome would be huge wind in the sails, while a defeat would not create a crisis.

Vinko highlighted the great danger that would loom if Hajduk had to play away at Gibraltar's Lincoln Red Imps on artificial turf in the first round. Such away trips, Marjan recalled using the example of the struggles of Rijeka and Crvena zvezda in Gibraltar, carry a huge burden because a victory is taken for granted, and every slip-up causes an earthquake.

Recalling the legendary historic clashes with Ajax from the 1990s in the UEFA Cup and the Champions League, Marjan emphasized that in a single match at Poljud everything is possible. Nevertheless, the pragmatic goal in Europe must be collecting points against the Swiss representative and the team from Gibraltar in order to win the six or seven points needed to advance from the group, whereby the entire European campaign must serve as a school for the future, not a hindrance to the fight for the domestic title.

sections.subtitle: Viewer participation and condemnation of the pyrotechnics incident
sections.screenshot_description: Host Marjan reads with visible disgust a viewer's question about the pyrotechnics incident at the derby.
sections.content:
In the closing part of the show, while waiting on air for midnight and the birthday of a loyal viewer, the hosts opened up space for comments from viewers directly from the chat. They commented on the television broadcast and commentator Igor Puškar, taking issue with his dramatization of the storm and openly calling for the suspension of the derby due to the waterlogged pitch.

The central topic of the viewers' questions was the incident orchestrated by visiting fans, Bad Blue Boys, who threw lit flares from the southwest stand toward the section designated for persons with disabilities beneath the scoreboard. Both Marjan and Vinko condemned the act without reservation, calling it an absolute civilizational rock bottom, cowardice, and a disgrace to the entire fan scene.

- **Criticism of media hypocrisy**: Vinko drew a parallel with the days of media outrage when Torcida damaged seats at the stadium in Velika Gorica, predicting that barely a few lines would be written about endangering the lives of persons with disabilities at Poljud.
- **The question of responsibility**: Marjan expressed disbelief toward those in the stand who mutely observed the throwing of pyrotechnics at the most vulnerable group of spectators, emphasizing that it is a pure criminal offense deserving the sharpest public and judicial condemnation.

iterations.theme: Viewers' questions: individual player statuses, title ambitions, and sign-off

sections.subtitle: Perception of Bamba's form and physical condition
sections.screenshot_description: Vinko Dubravica and Marjan discuss Bamba's form and reactions to his play
sections.content:
In the closing part of the show, the focus shifted to viewers' questions from the chat, and the first of them concerned Bamba's health condition and perceived progress. A question was posed as to whether a portion of the fans was prone to doubts or even relief when news emerged about his alleged injury at the national team camp. Vinko Dubravica openly admits that he personally was not at all happy about such rumors because he considers that Bamba has started playing significantly more serious and mature football than ever before in the white shirt.

Dubravica notes that Bamba's history of injuries—from knee and ankle to shoulder—made him cautious, because every time he catches a rhythm, a break of a month or two would follow that completely knocked him off balance. Marjan chimes in, emphasizing that Bamba possesses a specific energy with which he can bring complete havoc to the opponent's ranks in any 30 or 60 minutes. They conclude that he should be supported, his strengths utilized, and his flaws minimized, rather than being mocked from the stands.

sections.subtitle: Goalkeeping question: long-term trust in Silić
sections.screenshot_description: Marjan argues why Hajduk must endure Silić in the goalkeeping position
sections.content:
In the discussion, viewers also opened the question of the goalkeeping position, asking whether Silić should be removed from goal due to certain fluctuations and insecurities that could cost the team dearly in Europe and the league. Marjan resolutely opposes such an idea and points out that Silić is a club project that must be endured. He recalls that he was projected to be the number one already back in his junior days and that he possesses enormous potential despite occasional errors.

Vinko Dubravica supports that stance, drawing a parallel with the situation when Lučić fell into a series of errors, but emphasizes that Hajduk does not have a better and longer-term alternative at this moment. Dante Stipica is in the twilight of his career, while Silić is a young goalkeeper who must mature through pressure and daily work. Both agree that removing the young goalkeeper would cause the club many times more harm than good.

sections.subtitle: Assessment of the championship title race between Dinamo, Hajduk, and Rijeka
sections.screenshot_description: Analysis of the prospects for the championship title in the three-way race between Dinamo, Hajduk, and Rijeka
sections.content:
Commenting on the chances of winning the championship title, Marjan evaluates that Dinamo is still nominally the biggest favorite, primarily due to logistical strength, refereeing criteria, and the supporting apparatus that has brought them the advantage in crisis moments for years. However, he emphasizes that Hajduk has an exceptionally competitive squad that can stand toe-to-toe with the Zagreb rival on condition that it maintains a high level of focus.

As for Rijeka, the interlocutors consider that the team from Rujevica depends heavily on the individual form and fate of Frk, as well as possible winter transfers. Still, the key factor could be European wear and tear: since Dinamo and Hajduk are playing on two tracks, fatigue could open up space for Rijeka, but also for Osijek and Varaždin to snatch points from the favorites. Dubravica warns that the season is only at one quarter and that any early predictions are ungrateful.

sections.subtitle: Comment on the meeting between Luka Modrić and Marko Livaja and football anecdotes
sections.screenshot_description: Vinko Dubravica recounts an anecdote about Miki Rapaić and football friendship
sections.content:
A viewer's question referred to the meeting between Luka Modrić and Marko Livaja at Poljud after the national team match. Marjan describes that act as a completely natural and sportsmanlike gesture by two former national team teammates who won bronze together in Qatar. He adds that children took photos with Modrić and that rivalry among fans has nothing to do with the mutual relationships of professional athletes who have known each other since youth selections.

The discussion then drifted into more relaxed waters of reminiscing about iconic football figures. Vinko Dubravica recounts an anecdote about Miki Rapaić from his time playing in Turkey, when he asked a teammate to simulate a hard tackle on him during morning training just so he could avoid the exertion and go home to sleep after a night out. A similar story is also mentioned about Paul Gascoigne, who jumped over a fence looking for a ball and disappeared for a full 24 hours, with the conclusion that modern football chronically lacks such authentic characters.

sections.subtitle: Midnight birthday greeting and relaxed discussion with the audience
sections.screenshot_description: The hosts toast and wish a happy birthday to a viewer exactly at midnight
sections.content:
Exactly with the stroke of midnight, Marjan and Vinko Dubravica interrupt more serious analyses to fulfill an earlier promise and wish a happy birthday to a loyal viewer who follows the show under the nickname Stupa. Along with good wishes for health and happiness, they also wished him a Hajduk championship title at the end of the season. The relaxed conversation continued with interaction with the chat, in which the audience lined up questions about the atmosphere, TV broadcasts, and club topics.

They also touched upon the issue of sound manipulation in television broadcasts, commenting on differences in the loudness of fan groups depending on the channel broadcasting the derby. Marjan notes that media and production spins have been repeating for years, but that this does not bother them at all after a big victory. Both point out that despite exhaustion and hours of marathon broadcasting, it is nice to welcome a new day in a victorious mood.

sections.subtitle: Comparison of the roles and profiles of Šego and Marko Livaja
sections.screenshot_description: Marjan explains the tactical differences between the profiles of Šego and Marko Livaja
sections.content:
To a comment from the chat that faulted Marjan for alleged intolerance toward Šego and favoritism of Marko Livaja, the host responds with a direct tactical analysis. He repeats his stance that Šego, across a series of past matches, offered too little concrete output in relation to ball usage and that a single assist cannot completely erase missed sitters and constant offside runs.

Marjan points out that it makes no sense at all to compare Šego and Livaja because they are two diametrically opposite player profiles. While Šego brings high pressing, aggressive running, and dynamism, Livaja has unmatched technical control, ball shielding with his back to goal, and creativity. He concludes that the team needs both profiles, but the question remains open as to why the coaching staff does not use Livaja's qualities at all when the match is on the line and when it is necessary to retain possession.

sections.subtitle: Plans for the winter transfer window and final sign-off of the show
sections.screenshot_description: The hosts summarize squad needs for the winter and sign off the marathon live stream
sections.content:
The final viewer question concerned the team's needs in the upcoming winter transfer window. Vinko Dubravica points out that he would like to see reinforcement at the position of a classic center forward, because young loaned players like Martin have not so far shown enough character or fire to retain a spot in the team long-term. He believes that players without a real contribution should be sent back from loan if they do not wake up by mid-season.

Marjan adds that Hajduk has internal reserves at the center-back positions, citing Gabrić and Madunić as a center-back pairing with great potential, while the question of defensive midfielder depends on the form and adaptation of Donker. After more than three hours of program, the hosts thank the audience for watching and for the donations, announce new meetups midweek, and conclude the show with a message to the fans to proudly enjoy the big victory over the rival.
